newsitem.title: CROATIA: Independent Croatian radio wins licence - report.
newsitem.headline: Independent Croatian radio wins licence - report.

text.p: An independent Croatian radio station won a long legal wrangle with the government on Friday when the state telecommunications council awarded it a broadcasting licence.

"We got it! Radio 101 got its concession," reporter Zinka Bardic said in a live broadcast. There were mass protests in Zagreb last November when rightists in the Croatian government tried to shut down Radio 101.
Government authorities tried to silence the often critical Radio 101 last November when it awarded its frequency to a fledgling rival station, but protest rallies forced them to back off.

The telecommunications council decided on Friday that the radio could broadcast on its current 94.3 Megahertz frequency, but had to sort out an alleged ownership problem by October 31, Radio 101 said.
"We won the battle but not yet the war," Bardic said in an emotional call-in. No official comment on the decision of the council was immediately available.

The liberally-minded, youth-oriented Radio 101 has become a cultural trademark of the capital Zagreb, growing into a symbol of democracy in Croatia whose nationalist government silenced most independent media after coming to power in 1990.
